title: The Keys of the Kingdom
definition: The Keys of the Kingdom refer to the Church's Christ-given responsibility to confess the Gospel, receive believers, and exercise discipline according to His Word.
summary: The Keys of the Kingdom describe the authority Christ gives His Church to confess the Gospel, recognize true profession, and exercise discipline.
christFocus: Jesus Christ holds all authority and gives His Church responsibility to confess and guard the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The keys of the kingdom describe the church's responsibility to affirm or withhold visible recognition of Gospel confession through the Word and church discipline. Scripture connects the keys to proclaiming Christ, receiving repentant believers, and correcting unrepentant sin.

This doctrine is not permission for leaders to control salvation. Only Christ saves and judges finally, but the church must faithfully bear witness to the Gospel in its visible life.

Jesus gives authority to His church under His Word. The keys must be used humbly, carefully, and for the honor of Christ rather than human power.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Churches can either treat membership and discipline carelessly or misuse authority harshly. The keys of the kingdom protect Gospel clarity by showing that the church's visible witness matters.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Handle church authority with reverence and humility. Receive repentant believers gladly, take unrepentant sin seriously, and keep every act of recognition or correction submitted to Scripture and Christ.
